A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same theoretical work and contain 19 readable pages, including proofs, diagrams, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix. The material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 presents theoretical algorithms, complexity proofs, and a worked LP example, but no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis results.

after.justification: V2 remains a theoretical paper. Its revised proofs and retained worked example do not constitute empirical results.

M1.justification: The treewidth-based LP construction and counterfactual algorithm enumerating variable orders and response functions are retained. V2 corrects the complexity analysis and clarifies the construction without changing the algorithmic procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical training/evaluation tasks. The revised theoretical graph restriction in Theorem 9 is not an evaluated scenario.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods or baselines. References to other algorithms and complexity results remain theoretical context.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental protocols, data splits, evaluation metrics, training budgets, or testing procedures.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, or empirical supplementary analyses appear in either version. Example 6 retains the same illustrative LP construction and solution.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or empirical uncertainty estimates. Model probabilities are mathematical quantities.

E6.justification: Neither version reports empirical result entries or measured performance. Example 6's numerical probabilities and LP solution are unchanged; the revised complexity bounds are theoretical.

T1.justification: Theorem 11 corrects the response-function count from a bound of d^(n^2) to d^(d^n), increases the resulting runtime bound, and withdraws XP membership parameterized by n alone. Theorem 9 also replaces vertex-disjoint paths of length 2 with pairwise vertex-disjoint edges, aligning its statement with the retained reduction.

C1.justification: V1 claims both XP parameterized by n and FPT parameterized by n+d for linear counterfactual satisfiability. V2's contribution summary and Figure 1 retain only the latter guarantee, substantially narrowing a main contribution. The probabilistic treewidth claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds an explicit open question about polynomial-time solvability of linear counterfactual satisfiability with constantly many variables. This qualifies the tractability landscape where v1 had claimed a solution; the existing marginalization and broader-applicability discussions remain.

D1.justification: Theorem 5 explicitly clarifies that LP variables are created per distinct bag, since different tree nodes may share a bag, and that parents of omitted empty leaves serve as leaves. These document construction details without establishing an algorithm change.

R1.justification: V1's citation to the Fenton, Neil, and Constantinou review of The Book of Why is replaced by Pearl and Mackenzie's book itself. Other bibliography changes largely update metadata or numbering; the broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: V2 makes local wording and notation refinements throughout the preliminaries and proofs, names authors in related-work attributions, and revises the contribution summary and concluding discussion. The six-section organization and overall exposition remain.

P2.justification: Figure 1 removes the counterfactual XP-by-n label and adjusts the corresponding box. Problem-definition boxes and displayed LP constraints are reformatted, with associated page reflow. The existing worked-example diagrams are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 repairs a serious proof-to-claim mismatch in a central contribution: the corrected response-function count no longer supports v1's XP claim. Theorem 11, the contribution summary, Figure 1, and the new open question now reflect that limitation. Although the claimed tractability scope narrows, removing the unsupported guarantee substantially improves reliability. Theorem 9's statement is also brought into alignment with its construction.
